description: Node and cluster resource-pressure (sluggishness) dashboard for PCA: CPU, memory, disk and I/O-wait at cluster/node/pod level, plus saturation signals (CPU throttling, OOM kills, load-per-core). Uses node-exporter, cAdvisor/kubelet, and kube-prometheus recording rules.

options.content:
# PCA Node & Cluster Resource Health

Diagnoses **system sluggishness** caused by resource pressure – CPU, memory, disk, and I/O-wait – at three levels: **whole cluster**, **individual node**, and **individual pod**. It also surfaces the saturation signals that actually make things slow: **CPU throttling**, **OOM kills**, and **load average vs. cores**.

**How to read it**
- **Cluster overview** gauges: at-a-glance utilisation. Green = healthy, orange = warning, red = critical (CPU 80/90%, memory 85/95%, disk 80/90%, I/O-wait 5/10%, load-per-core 1/2).
- **Per-node**: compare nodes to find the hot one. A node pinned red on CPU/memory/I/O-wait or with load-per-core > 1–2 is a sluggishness source.
- **Per-pod**: top consumers (who is eating CPU/memory), CPU throttling (capped by its limit), OOM kills, and a `$pod` picker to compare a pod's usage against its requests/limits.

**Triage flow:** cluster gauge red → find the node(s) in Per-node → find the pod(s) on that node in Per-pod. High **I/O-wait** = disk is the bottleneck (check Disk IO %); high **throttling** = the pod is CPU-limited (raise its CPU limit); **OOMKilled** = raise the memory limit or fix a leak.

**Filters:** `$cluster`, `$node` (per-node), `$namespace` (default `pca`) and `$pod` (per-pod).

panels.description: Average CPU used across all nodes (1 - idle). Orange >=80%, red >=90% – the cluster is CPU-bound; find the hot node(s) in Per-node.
panels.title: Cluster CPU utilisation

panels.description: Used memory across all nodes (1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal). Orange >=85%, red >=95% – risk of OOM kills and swapping/sluggishness.
panels.title: Cluster memory utilisation

panels.description: Highest filesystem usage on any node/mount. Orange >=80%, red >=90% – a full disk stalls writes (HDFS/MinIO/Postgres/Kafka) and can crash services.
panels.title: Fullest filesystem

panels.description: Average CPU time waiting on disk I/O across nodes. Orange >=5%, red >=10% – the disk subsystem is the bottleneck; CPU is idle waiting for storage.
panels.title: Cluster I/O-wait

panels.description: Total 1-min load average / total logical cores. Orange >=1, red >=2 – more runnable work than CPUs = queuing/slowness.
panels.title: Load per core (cluster)

panels.description: Number of nodes reporting node-exporter metrics in this cluster.
panels.title: Nodes

panels.description: The busiest nodes by CPU right now. Orange ≥ 80%, red ≥ 90% – a node near 100% will throttle/queue its pods; check the Top pods CPU panel to see which pods are driving it, or reschedule/scale.
panels.title: Top nodes – CPU utilisation %

panels.description: The fullest nodes by memory right now. Orange ≥ 80%, red ≥ 90% – a node near 100% risks kernel OOM-kills of its pods; identify heavy pods (Top pods memory) or add capacity.
panels.title: Top nodes – memory utilisation %

panels.description: Absolute CPU cores consumed per node right now. Compare against each node's core count to spot imbalance across the cluster. Not threshold-coloured (core counts differ by node).
panels.title: Top nodes – CPU cores used

panels.description: Absolute memory used per node right now (total − available). Use with memory % to see both pressure and raw footprint. Not threshold-coloured (node sizes differ).
panels.title: Top nodes – memory used

panels.description: Nodes spending the most CPU time waiting on disk. Orange ≥ 10%, red ≥ 25% – high I/O-wait means storage is the bottleneck; see the disk I/O utilisation panel and the Disk/PVC consumers row.
panels.title: Top nodes – I/O-wait %

panels.description: Run-queue pressure normalised by core count (load1 / cores). Orange ≥ 1 (fully committed), red ≥ 2 (over-subscribed) – sustained > 1 means processes are waiting for CPU on that node.
panels.title: Top nodes – load per core

panels.description: Per-node CPU used (1 - idle). Dashed lines mark the 80%/90% thresholds. A node pinned near/over the red line is CPU-bound – drill into Per-pod to see which pods on it are heaviest.
panels.title: Node – CPU utilisation %

panels.description: Per-node used memory (1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal). Thresholds 85%/95%. A node near red is at OOM risk – pods there may be OOMKilled (see Per-pod).
panels.title: Node – memory utilisation %

panels.description: Per-node CPU time spent waiting on disk I/O. Thresholds 5%/10%. Sustained high I/O-wait = the node's disks cannot keep up; correlate with Disk IO % below and the storage pods (HDFS/MinIO/Kafka/Postgres).
panels.title: Node – I/O-wait %

panels.description: Per-node 1-min load average divided by that node's logical cores. Thresholds 1/2. > 1 per core = more runnable work than CPUs (queuing). Compare with CPU% – high load with moderate CPU often means I/O-wait. (Fixed: load1 is summed by instance so it matches the per-node core count.)
panels.title: Node – load average per core

panels.description: Per-node, per-mount filesystem usage. Thresholds 80%/90%. A mount near red will stop accepting writes – identify the node/mount and free space or expand the volume.
panels.title: Node – filesystem usage % (by mount)

panels.description: Fraction of time each disk device was busy (node_disk_io_time_seconds_total rate). ~100% = the device is saturated and is the bottleneck behind high I/O-wait. Correlate with the storage services on that node.
panels.title: Node – disk I/O utilisation % (by device)

panels.description: The 15 pods using the most CPU right now (cores). Use this to find who is driving a node's CPU% up. Not threshold-coloured (absolute cores vary by pod).
panels.title: Top pods – CPU (cores)

panels.description: The 15 pods using the most memory right now (working set). Watch pods approaching their memory limit – they are the OOM-kill candidates.
panels.title: Top pods – memory

panels.description: Pods being CPU-throttled (share of CFS periods throttled). Only pods with a CPU limit can throttle. Orange >=25%, red >=50% – a throttled pod is slow because it is capped; raise its CPU limit or reduce load.
panels.title: Top pods – CPU throttling %

panels.description: Pods whose most recent container termination was OOMKilled (out of memory). A series at 1 = that pod was OOM-killed – it hit its memory limit (or the node ran out). Fix by raising the memory limit or addressing a leak; correlate with node memory% above.
panels.title: Pods OOMKilled (last termination reason)

panels.description: For the pod(s) chosen in $pod: actual CPU usage vs its configured request and limit (cores). Usage riding the limit → expect throttling (see Top throttling); usage far below request → over-provisioned.
panels.title: Selected pod – CPU vs requests/limits

panels.description: For the pod(s) chosen in $pod: working-set memory vs its request and limit (bytes). Usage approaching the limit → OOM-kill risk; raise the limit or fix the leak.
panels.title: Selected pod – memory vs requests/limits

panels.description: The 15 pods closest to their CPU limit (usage / limit). Pods with no CPU limit are excluded. Orange >=80%, red >=90% – a pod near 100% of its CPU limit is being (or about to be) throttled; raise its limit or reduce load. Complements 'Top pods – CPU (cores)', which shows absolute usage.
panels.title: Top pods – CPU vs limit %

panels.description: The 15 pods closest to their memory limit (working set / limit). Pods with no memory limit are excluded. Orange >=80%, red >=90% – a pod near 100% of its memory limit is an OOM-kill candidate; raise its limit or fix the leak. Complements 'Top pods – memory', which shows absolute usage.
panels.title: Top pods – memory vs limit %

panels.description: Fullest node-local filesystems (root/ephemeral), by node:mount. Orange ≥ 80%, red ≥ 90% – a full node disk stops container writes, image pulls and logging. This is node-local storage; SAN-backed PVCs are in the PVC panels. On this embedded cluster the OpenEBS hostpath PVCs live on these same node filesystems, so this node-disk fullness is the true capacity limit for PVCs as well.
panels.title: Top nodes – filesystem usage % (node-local disk)

panels.description: Total real PVC disk usage per node, from the du-exporter mapped PVC→pod→node. Shows which nodes carry the heaviest local-volume load. NOTE: this is an embedded cluster using the OpenEBS hostpath provisioner – PVCs are directories on the node's local disk, so kubelet_volume_stats_* reports the whole node filesystem for EVERY PVC (identical values). This panel instead uses the openebs_hostpath_volume_used_bytes du-exporter, which measures real per-volume usage.

targets.expr:
topk(15, sum by (node) (
(
openebs_hostpath_volume_used_bytes
  * on(persistentvolume) group_left(namespace, persistentvolumeclaim)
    label_replace(kube_persistentvolumeclaim_info{namespace=~"$namespace"}, "persistentvolume", "$1", "volumename", "(.+)")
)
  * on(namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) group_left(node)
    max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim, node) (
      kube_pod_spec_volumes_persistentvolumeclaims_info
        * on(namespace, pod) group_left(node) kube_pod_info
    )
))

panels.title: Top nodes – PVC disk usage (bytes)

panels.description: The pods whose PVCs consume the most real disk, from the du-exporter mapped PVC→pod. Finds the storage-hungry workloads. NOTE: this is an embedded cluster using the OpenEBS hostpath provisioner – PVCs are directories on the node's local disk, so kubelet_volume_stats_* reports the whole node filesystem for EVERY PVC (identical values). This panel instead uses the openebs_hostpath_volume_used_bytes du-exporter, which measures real per-volume usage.
panels.title: Top pods – PVC disk usage (bytes)

panels.description: Each PVC's real usage as a share of the node disk it lives on (openebs du-exporter used / kubelet-reported filesystem capacity). On hostpath there is no per-PVC quota, so 'how full is the PVC' is not a real number – the binding limit is node-disk fullness (see the node filesystem panel). This shows which PVCs dominate a node's disk. Orange ≥ 60%, red ≥ 80% of a single disk. NOTE: this is an embedded cluster using the OpenEBS hostpath provisioner – PVCs are directories on the node's local disk, so kubelet_volume_stats_* reports the whole node filesystem for EVERY PVC (identical values). This panel instead uses the openebs_hostpath_volume_used_bytes du-exporter, which measures real per-volume usage.

targets.expr:
topk(15, 100 * (
openebs_hostpath_volume_used_bytes
  * on(persistentvolume) group_left(namespace, persistentvolumeclaim)
    label_replace(kube_persistentvolumeclaim_info{namespace=~"$namespace"}, "persistentvolume", "$1", "volumename", "(.+)")
) / on(namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) group_left() kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes)

panels.title: Top PVCs – % of node disk consumed

panels.description: Real disk consumed per PVC, from the per-directory du-exporter (openebs_hostpath_volume_used_bytes) mapped to its PVC name. Pair with the node filesystem panel to see headroom. NOTE: this is an embedded cluster using the OpenEBS hostpath provisioner – PVCs are directories on the node's local disk, so kubelet_volume_stats_* reports the whole node filesystem for EVERY PVC (identical values). This panel instead uses the openebs_hostpath_volume_used_bytes du-exporter, which measures real per-volume usage.

targets.expr:
topk(15, sum by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (
openebs_hostpath_volume_used_bytes
  * on(persistentvolume) group_left(namespace, persistentvolumeclaim)
    label_replace(kube_persistentvolumeclaim_info{namespace=~"$namespace"}, "persistentvolume", "$1", "volumename", "(.+)")
))

panels.title: Top PVCs – used bytes

title: PCA Node & Cluster Resource Health
